newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-TIME UP FOR TIME-OUTS IN BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TIME UP FOR TIME-OUTS IN BRAZIL.

text.p: The experiment of time-outs in soccer came to an end on Friday when the Sao Paulo football federation (FPF) announced they would no longer be allowed in the Sao Paulo championship.
An FPF spokeswoman said the experiment had been suspended on the orders of soccer's world governing body FIFA because it was not in the rules of the game.
The experiment, which began last year, allowed coaches the option of calling a three-minute time-out at any moment between the 22nd and 25th minutes of the half in which their team had kicked off.
This year the experiment was widened to allow a time-out at any time before the 30th minute of the half.

However, the rules caused confusion on the first day of the season when a Canadian official brought in to referee the match between Sao Jose and Palmeiras refused to allow time-outs on the basis that they were not sanctioned under international rules.
